# Blocks catalog (`@mn/blocks` v0.52.0)

<!-- Generated by `npm run catalog` from scripts/catalog.mjs. Do not edit by hand. -->

Every exported piece, one line each. Read this instead of the source; use a block
before writing your own. Missing an option? Add it to the block here, never fork it into an app.

## How apps use it

- **Install (client):** `npm install "@mn/blocks@github:mikeylikesitnot-rgb/blocks#v0.52.0"`. A client-only app needs nothing else.
- **Server pieces** (`@mn/blocks/server`, `@mn/blocks/email`): the app also installs `jose bcryptjs express-rate-limit nodemailer` (optional peers); `@mn/blocks/server/richtext` needs `sanitize-html` instead; `@mn/blocks/server/qa` needs `sanitize-html express-rate-limit` (plus `better-sqlite3` or `pg`, which the app already has); `@mn/blocks/browser` needs `playwright-core`.
- **Editor** (`@mn/blocks/editor`): the app also installs `@tiptap/react @tiptap/pm @tiptap/starter-kit`.
- **CSS:** `import '@mn/blocks/kit.css'` once (brings tokens.css), before the app's own CSS. With Tailwind, put it in the components layer (`@import "@mn/blocks/kit.css" layer(components);`) so utilities passed as `className` win. The editor imports its own `editor.css`. Optional `import '@mn/blocks/premium.css'` right after kit.css (same layer) switches to the premium look: blue accent, cool greys, system font, true-black dark.
- **Wrap** the app in `<OverlayProvider>` (confirm, alert, toasts); add `class="mk-root"` to `<body>` for base font and colours (optional).
- **Theme:** override tokens after the import, e.g. `:root { --mk-primary: #0f766e; --mk-primary-hover: #115e59; }`; set the same tokens in the dark blocks too. Never edit kit CSS; classes stay `mk-*`.
- **Dark mode** follows the OS; force with `<html data-theme="light|dark">` or `useTheme()`.

Props: ({tags, scriptUrls}); cleanRichHtml(html, {tags}). `import { installRichTrustedTypes, cleanRichHtml, cleanRichNodes, safeHref, RICH_TAGS, GOOGLE_GSI_URL } from '@mn/blocks/editor'`

Props: (dir, {commits}) — commits from changelogCommits fill links.commit. `import { readChangelog, CHANGELOG_ID, CHANGELOG_IMAGE } from '@mn/blocks/server'`
- **changelogCommits**: The commit that added each changelog/<id>/entry.json ({id: hash}); {} without git, so run it at deploy and ship the result. Props: (repoDir, {dir "changelog"}). `import { changelogCommits } from '@mn/blocks/server'`

### Server: saved UI choices

- **pgUiPrefStore** (+ uiPrefSchemaSql, memoryUiPrefStore): Stores for uiPrefsRouter: Postgres (one JSONB row per person and key, plus the idempotent CREATE TABLE) and in-memory for tests; an app with its own table passes {get, set} instead. ### Server: crypto

- **encrypt** (+ decrypt): AES-256-GCM for small stored secrets, keyed from an existing secret. Props: (text, secret, salt). `import { encrypt, decrypt } from '@mn/blocks/server'`

### Server: rich text (needs sanitize-html)

- **sanitizeRich** (+ NOTE_TAGS, EDITOR_TAGS): Cleans editor HTML on the server before it is stored: allowlisted tags only, links http/https/mailto/tel with rel=noopener, script/style text dropped, <div>/<b>/<i> become <p>/<strong>/<em>; needs the optional peer sanitize-html. Props: (value, {tags EDITOR_TAGS | NOTE_TAGS | [...], plainText 'html' | 'keep' (no tags: stored as typed)}); null stays null. `import { sanitizeRich, NOTE_TAGS, EDITOR_TAGS } from '@mn/blocks/server/richtext'`
- **cleanRich** (+ MAX_RICH_LENGTH): sanitizeRich for a column where no note is NULL: blank ("", "<p></p>", "&nbsp;") becomes null, else cleaned and trimmed, with a length check. Props: (value, {tags, plainText, maxLength 20000}) -> {value, tooLong}. `import { cleanRich, MAX_RICH_LENGTH } from '@mn/blocks/server/richtext'`
- **isBlankRich** (+ richToPlain, looksLikeHtml, HTML_TAG): Server names for the editor value helpers: blank check, one-line plain text, and the "is this HTML or plain text" test RichText/toRichHtml use. Props: (html). `import { isBlankRich, richToPlain, looksLikeHtml, HTML_TAG } from '@mn/blocks/server/richtext'`

## `@mn/blocks/server/qa`

### Server: Q&A board (needs sanitize-html, express-rate-limit)

- **qaRouter** (+ QA_SORTS, QA_LIMITS, normalizeTag): Express router for QaBoard (mount after express.json(), behind requireAuth or optionalAuth): questions, answers, ±1 votes (one per person, none on your own post), accepted answer (asker only), plain-text comments, tags, sort/tag (any ticked)/search/pages, GET /me; authors edit/delete their own, moderators any and close/reopen; a question with answers is deleted only by a moderator; bodies cleaned with cleanRich; writes rate-limited per person and per kind (posts, votes, comments; signed-out callers get 401 first); author names never fall back to the email; 400s carry {errors: {field}}. Props: {store, user (req) => {id, name}, moderator (req) => bool, moderatorRoles ['admin'], board ('main' | req => name), limits {posts 20, votes 60, comments 30} per 15 min, rateLimitKey (req => client id behind a proxy), limiter (one middleware for all, or false), onEvent(type 'question'|'answer'|'comment'|'accept', data, req), onError}. `import { qaRouter, QA_SORTS, QA_LIMITS, normalizeTag } from '@mn/blocks/server/qa'`
- **pgQaStore** (+ qaSchemaSql, sqliteQaStore, qaSqliteSchemaSql, memoryQaStore): Stores for qaRouter: Postgres (questions, answers, comments, votes, views tables with a configurable prefix; tags as text[] with a GIN index, full-text search; plus the idempotent CREATE TABLE SQL), SQLite on a better-sqlite3 Database (creates its tables itself; tags as JSON, word search; turn on foreign_keys) and in-memory for tests and demos. Props: (pool, {prefix 'qa_'}); qaSchemaSql({prefix}); sqliteQaStore(db, {prefix, now}); memoryQaStore({now}). `import { pgQaStore, qaSchemaSql, sqliteQaStore, qaSqliteSchemaSql, memoryQaStore } from '@mn/blocks/server/qa'`

**`@mn/blocks/server/ui-prefs`**: uiPrefsRouter and its stores alone (needs only Express; no jose or bcrypt).

## `@mn/blocks/browser`

### Server: browser (needs playwright-core; Mac jobs only)

- **withPage**: Opens a NEW tab in the already-running, already-logged-in automation Chrome, goes to url, runs fn(page), always closes the tab and disconnects (Chrome and the user's tabs are never touched); returns fn's result. Props: (url, fn(page), {port 9222, host, timeoutMs, waitUntil, navTimeoutMs}). `import { withPage } from '@mn/blocks/browser'`
- **connectChrome**: Connects Playwright to the running Chrome over CDP (chromium.connectOverCDP); clear errors for a missing playwright-core and for Chrome not running with remote debugging. browser.close() only disconnects. Props: ({port 9222, host '127.0.0.1', timeoutMs}) -> {browser, context}. `import { connectChrome } from '@mn/blocks/browser'`
- **downloadText**: Waits for the download a trigger starts (e.g. clicking Export) and returns its text. Props: (page, trigger(page), {timeoutMs}) -> {fileName, text}. `import { downloadText } from '@mn/blocks/browser'`
- **needsLogin**: True when the page is a sign-in page (URL contains login/signin/sign-in, or a password field), so a job reports "log in to the automation profile" instead of scraping it. Props: (page, {urlIncludes}). `import { needsLogin } from '@mn/blocks/browser'`
- **chromeCommand** (+ chromeArgs, DEFAULT_PORT, DEFAULT_PROFILE_DIR): The command to start the automation Chrome (dedicated profile, debug port bound to 127.0.0.1; Chrome 136+ ignores the port on the default profile); chromeArgs gives {command, args}. Props: ({port 9222, profileDir '~/ChromeAutomation', chromePath}). `import { chromeCommand, chromeArgs, DEFAULT_PORT, DEFAULT_PROFILE_DIR } from '@mn/blocks/browser'`

## `@mn/blocks/siteapi`

### Server: siteapi (any website to an API; no deps, captureHar needs playwright-core)

- **siteFetch** (+ SiteApiError): Polite JSON client for one site's internal API: one request at a time with minGap between, cookie/token from ~/.config/siteapi/<site>.env, SiteApiError with .expired on 401/403 or an HTML page (logged out, bot wall). Props: ({base, site, minGap 1000, headers (object or (env) => object), timeoutMs, env}) -> {get(path, params), post(path, body, params), call(method, path, {params, body, headers}), env}. `import { siteFetch, SiteApiError } from '@mn/blocks/siteapi'`
- **readSiteEnv** (+ siteEnvPath): A site's secrets: KEY=value lines from ~/.config/siteapi/<site>.env, with <SITE>_KEY env vars on top. Props: (site, {home, env}). `import { readSiteEnv, siteEnvPath } from '@mn/blocks/siteapi'`
- **analyzeHar** (+ normPath, jsonShape): Ranks the JSON endpoints in a HAR by how likely they hold the page's data (text you saw on the page wins), groups ids/VINs into {id}, labels GraphQL ops, skips analytics and static files, and reports JSON embedded in HTML (__NEXT_DATA__, ld+json). Props: (har, {find [], allHosts}) -> {pageHost, endpoints [{n, endpoint, status, queryKeys, authHeaders, found, shape, sample, request}], embedded}. `import { analyzeHar, normPath, jsonShape } from '@mn/blocks/siteapi'`
- **probeRequest**: Replays a captured request with fewer headers (none, browser, + cookies, full) and names the least that still returns JSON. Props: (request, {fetch}) -> {levels, minimum, extraHeaders}. `import { probeRequest } from '@mn/blocks/siteapi'`
- **captureHar**: Records a page's traffic (requests + JSON/HTML bodies) as a HAR: in a new tab of the signed-in automation Chrome (chrome: true, tab closed after) or a fresh installed-Chrome launch; browseMs keeps it open for a person to log in or click. Props: (url, {chrome, headed, browseMs, waitMs, scroll, port}). `import { captureHar } from '@mn/blocks/siteapi'`

## `@mn/blocks/server/spam`

### Server: contact-form spam checks (no deps)

- **spamCheck** (+ botReason, contentReason, SPAM_MAYBE_HUMAN): Every check in order: bots (filled honeypot, no time-to-fill value, under minMs) then content (fake 555-01xx phone, off-site link, sales pitch); returns the reason and the phrase groups the message hit, or null. The app decides what a hit does (keep as spam, skip alerts, show a fix-it page). Props: ({honeypot, elapsedMs, name, phone, message}, {minMs 3000, allowHosts [], phrases}) -> {reason honeypot|no-timing|too-fast|fake-phone|link|sales-pitch, groups} | null. `import { spamCheck, botReason, contentReason, SPAM_MAYBE_HUMAN } from '@mn/blocks/server/spam'`
- **isSalesPitch** (+ pitchGroups, SPAM_PHRASES): Vendor-pitch check on message wording: at least 2 different phrase groups (call, opt-out, money, marketing, ai, target, partner, intro), one of them strong. The list is server/spamPhrases.json, PCRE-compatible so PHP sites read the same file. Props: (text, {phrases}) -> bool; pitchGroups(text) -> [group]. `import { isSalesPitch, pitchGroups, SPAM_PHRASES } from '@mn/blocks/server/spam'`
- **hasLink** (+ isFakePhone): Link check (http(s)://, www., [url, <a ) that lets links to your own hosts and their subdomains through; isFakePhone flags the fictional 555-0100..0199 range in any format. Props: (text, {allowHosts []}); isFakePhone(phone). `import { hasLink, isFakePhone } from '@mn/blocks/server/spam'`

## `@mn/blocks/desktop-update`

### Desktop apps: auto update (Electron main, no other deps)

- **createUpdater** (+ UPDATE_MODES): Checks the app's GitHub Releases (private repos with a read-only token), downloads in the background (size + sha256 checked) and installs: Windows runs the NSIS installer silently, macOS swaps the .app from the release .zip after quit (works unsigned; no Squirrel). Modes auto (install on quit, or Restart now) / notify / off; checks 15s after start and every 6h. From CommonJS: `await import('@mn/blocks/desktop-update')`. Props: ({app, repo 'owner/name', getToken, getMode () => auto|notify|off, onState({status idle|checking|up-to-date|available|downloading|ready|error, current, latest, notes, url, progress, canInstall, error, errorCode}), intervalHours (6), log}) -> {start, stop, check({manual}), download, install({relaunch}), state}. `import { createUpdater, UPDATE_MODES } from '@mn/blocks/desktop-update'`
- **tokenStore**: Keeps the GitHub token encrypted with Electron safeStorage in one file (mode 600). Props: ({safeStorage, file}) -> {get, set(token) ('' removes), has, encrypted() (false: OS has no encryption, stored as plain text)}. `import { tokenStore } from '@mn/blocks/desktop-update'`
- **pickAsset** (+ appBundlePath, SWAP_SCRIPT): Which release file fits this computer (.exe on Windows, .zip on macOS, by arch); the running .app path; the swap script. Props: (assets, {platform, arch}). `import { pickAsset, appBundlePath, SWAP_SCRIPT } from '@mn/blocks/desktop-update'`
- **compareVersions** (+ isNewer): Semver-ish compare; "v1.10.0" > "1.9.3", pre-releases sort first. Props: (a, b) -> -1|0|1. `import { compareVersions, isNewer } from '@mn/blocks/desktop-update'`

**`@mn/blocks/email`**: just the email templates, no Express or nodemailer needed.

## Ops scripts (`node_modules/@mn/blocks/ops/`)

- **backup.sh**: Nightly VPS backup: Postgres dump + files + folders in one restic snapshot, encrypted to Google Drive via rclone, healthchecks.io pings, retries, keep rules that really delete, weekly restore test into a scratch database, local copies. Use: deploy copies it to the VPS; cron runs `backup.sh <config>` (config keys in the header: NAME, RESTIC_REPOSITORY, RESTIC_PASSWORD_FILE, HC_PING_URL, DB_CONTAINER, DB_FORMAT, DB_FILE, DB_CHECK_TABLE, RESTORE_TEST_TABLES, COPY_FILES, BACKUP_PATHS, KEEP_*); `RESTORE_TEST=1` runs the restore test now.
- **automation-chrome.sh**: Starts the dedicated automation Chrome (profile ~/ChromeAutomation, debug port bound to 127.0.0.1); idempotent: exits 0 if the port already answers and is this profile (DevToolsActivePort matches), 1 if another Chrome has the port; on macOS starts Chrome with `open -na` so it survives a launchd job exiting. Use: run `ops/automation-chrome.sh` (env PORT, PROFILE_DIR, CHROME) from launchd or by hand; sign in to your sites in that window once; jobs then use @mn/blocks/browser.
- **automation-chrome.ps1**: Windows twin of automation-chrome.sh (same checks, Program Files or per-user Chrome). Use: `powershell -File automation-chrome.ps1 [-Port 9222] [-ProfileDir C:\path]`.
- **desktop-release.mjs**: Releases an Electron app for desktop-update (run on the Mac): checks a clean, up-to-date tree, sets the version, builds macOS dmg + zip and Windows NSIS (npm run dist:win if present), commits "Release X", tags vX, pushes, and `gh release create` with the files; a failed build commits nothing, a failed push undoes the local commit and tag. Use: `node node_modules/@mn/blocks/ops/desktop-release.mjs <patch|minor|major|x.y.z> [--notes-file f | --notes "..."] [--mac] [--win] [--draft] [--dry-run]` from the app folder.
- **apps.mjs**: Installs and updates Michael's own apps on this computer from ops/apps.json: electron-release apps from their latest GitHub release (macOS .zip swapped into /Applications after a sha256 check, reopened if it was running; Windows NSIS .exe run silently), script-repo apps cloned or pulled (--ff-only, never with local changes) into ~/apps or C:\apps and then their per-OS hook (.sh / .ps1) run; install = missing or behind, update = installed and behind, --force anyway; all GitHub access through gh; --json for apps (Project Hub's Apps page). Use: `node ops/apps.mjs status|install|update [name|all] [--json [--progress]] [--force] [--manifest f] [--apps-dir d]` (--progress: steps to stderr with --json, for a live UI like AppShelf); add an app = one entry in ops/apps.json (name, kind, repo, product or branch + hook {darwin, win32}, platforms, folder when the apps-folder name differs); hooks run with no terminal and must never prompt.
- **ext-update.sh**: Keeps unpacked Chrome/Edge extensions current: for each line `<name> <git url> <branch> <folder|.> [build command]` in ~/.config/mn-ext-update/extensions, shallow-fetches the branch and copies the folder (with a build command: runs it first and copies its output folder) to ~/.mn-extensions/<name> when manifest.json "version" changed (your git login, so private repos work); `install` schedules it every 30 min (launchd / Task Scheduler), one run at a time, log in ~/.mn-extensions/.bin/ext-update.log. Use: `ops/ext-update.sh run|install|uninstall|list [config]`; load ~/.mn-extensions/<name> once with Load unpacked (keep "key" in the manifest), then startExtUpdate reloads it on each new version.
- **changelog-shot.mjs**: Before/after screenshots for a changelog entry: signs in to the LOCAL app (refuses any other address), opens each page at 1280px (and 390px with --phone), saves <name>-N.jpg (JPEG q80) and writes them into <out>/entry.json shots. Use: `node node_modules/@mn/blocks/ops/changelog-shot.mjs --base http://localhost:5173 --out changelog/<id> --name before|after [--login 'POST /api/auth/dev-login {"role":"admin"}'] [--phone] [--hide <css>] [--wait <css>] [--full] /page ...`; needs Playwright in the app.
- **siteapi.mjs**: Find a website's internal JSON API: capture traffic (fresh browser, or --chrome for the signed-in automation Chrome), rank the endpoints, probe the least auth each needs; files in ~/.config/siteapi/out/<site>/ (outside every repo, they hold cookies). Used by the /siteapi skill. Use: `node ops/siteapi.mjs capture <url> --site <name> [--chrome] [--browse 120]`, `analyze <site> [--find text]...`, `probe <site> <n>`.
